subproblem.title: Projection norm and differential of the polar angle in Q
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a 2-dimensional linear subspace with orthogonal projection π := Q.starProjection, and let a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a,e⟩ = 0. Put f(y) := arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩). Then (i) |πy|² = ⟨y,a⟩² + ⟨y,e⟩² for every y ∈ ℝ^P. (ii) For every x with ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, f is C¹ on a neighbourhood of x and Df(x)v = ⟨⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a, v⟩/|πx|² for every v ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → (∀ y : Euclid P, ‖Q.starProjection y‖ ^ 2 = inner ℝ y a ^ 2 + inner ℝ y e ^ 2) ∧ ∀ x : Euclid P, 0 < inner ℝ x a → ContDiffAt ℝ 1 (fun y : Euclid P => Real.arctan (inner ℝ y e / inner ℝ y a)) x ∧ ∀ v : Euclid P, fderiv ℝ (fun y : Euclid P => Real.arctan (inner ℝ y e / inner ℝ y a)) x v = inner ℝ (inner ℝ x a • e - inner ℝ x e • a) v / ‖Q.starProjection x‖ ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 3 of the parent proof.
Notation: π := Q.starProjection; for a fixed x write α := ⟨x,a⟩ and β := ⟨x,e⟩.
1. (Orthonormal basis of Q.) ⟨a,a⟩ = |a|² = 1, ⟨e,e⟩ = 1 and ⟨a,e⟩ = ⟨e,a⟩ = 0, so the family (a, e) is orthonormal and hence linearly independent. span{a, e} ⊆ Q because a, e ∈ Q, and it has dimension 2 = finrank Q. Therefore span{a, e} = Q (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq, with finrank_span_eq_card).
2. (Formula for π.) Fix y and put w := ⟨y,a⟩a + ⟨y,e⟩e ∈ Q. Then ⟨y − w, a⟩ = ⟨y,a⟩ − ⟨y,a⟩⟨a,a⟩ − ⟨y,e⟩⟨e,a⟩ = 0, and likewise ⟨y − w, e⟩ = ⟨y,e⟩ − ⟨y,a⟩⟨a,e⟩ − ⟨y,e⟩⟨e,e⟩ = 0. The vectors orthogonal to y − w form a subspace containing a and e, so they contain span{a,e} = Q. By the characterization of the orthogonal projection (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero), πy = w.
3. ((i)) |πy|² = ⟨w,w⟩ = ⟨y,a⟩²⟨a,a⟩ + 2⟨y,a⟩⟨y,e⟩⟨a,e⟩ + ⟨y,e⟩²⟨e,e⟩ = ⟨y,a⟩² + ⟨y,e⟩².
4. ((ii) Smoothness.) Let α > 0. The maps y ↦ ⟨y,a⟩ and y ↦ ⟨y,e⟩ are continuous linear, hence C^∞, with derivatives v ↦ ⟨v,a⟩ and v ↦ ⟨v,e⟩. Since ⟨x,a⟩ ≠ 0, y ↦ ⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩ is C^∞ at x (ContDiffAt.div). arctan is C^∞ (Real.contDiff_arctan), so f is C¹ at x.
5. ((ii) Derivative.) Write ⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩ = ⟨y,e⟩·(⟨y,a⟩)⁻¹. The derivative of t ↦ t⁻¹ at α is −1/α² (hasDerivAt_inv). By the chain and product rules, D(⟨·,e⟩/⟨·,a⟩)(x)v = β·(−⟨v,a⟩/α²) + α⁻¹⟨v,e⟩ = (α⟨v,e⟩ − β⟨v,a⟩)/α². Since arctan'(t) = 1/(1 + t²) (Real.hasDerivAt_arctan), the chain rule at t = β/α gives Df(x)v = (α⟨v,e⟩ − β⟨v,a⟩)/(α²(1 + β²/α²)) = (α⟨v,e⟩ − β⟨v,a⟩)/(α² + β²).
6. The numerator is ⟨αe − βa, v⟩ = ⟨⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a, v⟩ by symmetry of the real inner product. By (i) the denominator is α² + β² = |πx|², which is > 0. Hence fderiv f x v = ⟨⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a, v⟩/|Q.starProjection x|². ∎
proof_key_steps: (a, e) is an orthonormal basis of Q: it is independent and finrank Q = 2.
On ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, f = arctan(⟨·,e⟩/⟨·,a⟩) is C¹ at x.
Quotient and chain rules: Df(x)v = (⟨x,a⟩⟨v,e⟩ − ⟨x,e⟩⟨v,a⟩)/(⟨x,a⟩² + ⟨x,e⟩²) = ⟨Ax, v⟩/|πx|².

audit.reason: All geometric hypotheses appear in both statements. Orthonormality and finrank two establish the projection formula; the quotient and arctan chain rules give the exact differential. Positive inner product with a ensures the required denominators are nonzero. No circular dependency occurs.

subproblem.title: Conical C¹ cutoff around a subspace
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P with orthogonal projection π := Q.starProjection, and let s > 0. Then there is ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with four properties. (a) ζ is C¹ on a neighbourhood of every x ≠ 0. (b) ζ(x) = 1 whenever x ≠ 0 and |x − πx| ≤ (s/2)|x|. (c) ζ(x) = 0 whenever x ≠ 0 and s|x| ≤ |x − πx|. (d) Dζ(x) = 0 whenever x ≠ 0 and either |x − πx| < (s/2)|x| or s|x| < |x − πx|.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (s : ℝ), 0 < s → ∃ ζ : Euclid P → ℝ, (∀ x : Euclid P, x ≠ 0 → ContDiffAt ℝ 1 ζ x) ∧ (∀ x : Euclid P, x ≠ 0 → ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ ≤ s / 2 * ‖x‖ → ζ x = 1) ∧ (∀ x : Euclid P, x ≠ 0 → s * ‖x‖ ≤ ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ → ζ x = 0) ∧ (∀ x : Euclid P, x ≠ 0 → (‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ < s / 2 * ‖x‖ ∨ s * ‖x‖ < ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖) → fderiv ℝ ζ x = 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof.
Notation: π := Q.starProjection and q(y) := y − πy.
1. (Definition.) Let u(y) := |q(y)|²/(s²|y|²) and ζ(y) := smoothTransition((4/3)(1 − u(y))). Here Real.smoothTransition is Mathlib's C^∞ function with smoothTransition(t) = 0 for t ≤ 0 and smoothTransition(t) = 1 for t ≥ 1. The value at y = 0 plays no role.
2. ((a) Smoothness off 0.) q is a continuous linear map, so y ↦ |q(y)|² is C^∞ (ContDiff.norm_sq). The map y ↦ s²|y|² is C^∞ (contDiff_norm_sq), and at x ≠ 0 its value s²|x|² is nonzero because s > 0. Hence u is C^∞ at x (ContDiffAt.div), and so is y ↦ (4/3)(1 − u(y)). Since smoothTransition is C^∞ (Real.smoothTransition.contDiffAt), ζ is C^∞, in particular C¹, at x.
3. ((b)) Let x ≠ 0 with |q(x)| ≤ (s/2)|x|. Both sides are ≥ 0, so |q(x)|² ≤ (s²/4)|x|². Dividing by s²|x|² > 0 gives u(x) ≤ 1/4. Then (4/3)(1 − u(x)) ≥ (4/3)(3/4) = 1, so ζ(x) = 1 (Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le).
4. ((c)) Let x ≠ 0 with s|x| ≤ |q(x)|. Then s²|x|² ≤ |q(x)|², so u(x) ≥ 1 and (4/3)(1 − u(x)) ≤ 0. Hence ζ(x) = 0 (Real.smoothTransition.zero_of_nonpos).
5. ((d), first case.) Let x ≠ 0 with |q(x)| < (s/2)|x|. Let V := {y : y ≠ 0 and |q(y)| < (s/2)|y|}. V is open: it is the intersection of the open set {y ≠ 0} with a strict inequality between the continuous functions y ↦ |q(y)| and y ↦ (s/2)|y|. V contains x, and ζ = 1 on V by (b). So ζ agrees with the constant 1 on a neighbourhood of x, and Dζ(x) = 0 (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq, fderiv_const_apply).
6. ((d), second case.) Let x ≠ 0 with s|x| < |q(x)|. The set V' := {y : s|y| < |q(y)|} is open and contains x. Every y ∈ V' is nonzero, because at y = 0 both sides equal 0. So ζ = 0 on V' by (c), and Dζ(x) = 0.
7. Hence ζ satisfies (a)–(d). ∎
proof_key_steps: Define ζ := smoothTransition((4/3)(1 − |q|²/(s²|y|²))) with q = id − π.
u = |q|²/(s²|y|²) is C^∞ away from 0, so ζ is C¹ at every x ≠ 0.
|q| ≤ (s/2)|x| gives u ≤ 1/4 and ζ = 1; |q| ≥ s|x| gives u ≥ 1 and ζ = 0.
ζ is constant on the open sets {y ≠ 0, |q(y)| < (s/2)|y|} and {s|y| < |q(y)|}, so Dζ(x) = 0 there.

audit.reason: The explicit smoothTransition construction proves all four stated properties. Positivity of s and nonzero x justify division and squaring inequalities. Both strict derivative-zero regions are open regions of constancy; the origin is correctly excluded. The proof is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: Tangential divergence of the rotation field g·A of a plane
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P, a, e, x ∈ ℝ^P, and let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be differentiable at x. Put A y := ⟨y,a⟩e − ⟨y,e⟩a and X(y) := g(y)·A y. Let T := approxTangentPlane n M x and let p := T.starProjection be the orthogonal projection onto T. Then tangentialDivergence n M X x = trace(p ∘ DX(x)) equals Dg(x)(p(A x)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (a e x : Euclid P) (g : Euclid P → ℝ), DifferentiableAt ℝ g x → tangentialDivergence n M (fun y : Euclid P => g y • (inner ℝ y a • e - inner ℝ y e • a)) x = fderiv ℝ g x ((approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection (inner ℝ x a • e - inner ℝ x e • a))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, 2.3: div_M X(x) = trace(p_{T_xM} ∘ DX(x))).
Conventions: ⟨·,·⟩ is the symmetric real inner product of ℝ^P; T := approxTangentPlane n M x; p := T.starProjection, the orthogonal projection onto T; A y := ⟨y,a⟩e − ⟨y,e⟩a; X(y) := g(y)·A y.
1. (A is linear and skew.) A is the continuous linear map (innerSL ℝ a).smulRight e − (innerSL ℝ e).smulRight a, using ⟨a,y⟩ = ⟨y,a⟩. For every w ∈ ℝ^P, ⟨w, A w⟩ = ⟨w,a⟩⟨w,e⟩ − ⟨w,e⟩⟨w,a⟩ = 0.
2. (Derivative of X.) g has derivative Dg(x) at x, and the linear map A is its own derivative. By the product rule for a scalar function times a vector function (HasFDerivAt.fun_smul), X is differentiable at x with DX(x) = g(x)·A + Dg(x)(·)·A x. That is, DX(x)u = g(x)·A u + Dg(x)(u)·A x for all u.
3. (Splitting the trace.) By definition, tangentialDivergence n M X x = tr(p ∘ DX(x)). Since p is linear, p ∘ DX(x) = g(x)·(p ∘ A) + R with R u := Dg(x)(u)·p(A x). By linearity of the trace, tr(p ∘ DX(x)) = g(x)·tr(p ∘ A) + tr R.
4. (Rank-one term.) R is the rank-one map u ↦ L(u)·w with L := Dg(x) and w := p(A x), and its trace is L(w) (LinearMap.trace_smulRight). Hence tr R = Dg(x)(p(A x)).
5. (tr(p ∘ A) = 0.) p is idempotent: for every u, p u ∈ T and p fixes T, so p(p u) = p u (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem, Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff). Hence tr(p∘A) = tr(p∘(p∘A)), which equals tr((p∘A)∘p) by cyclicity of the trace (LinearMap.trace_comp_comm'). Let (b_i) be an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P (stdOrthonormalBasis). Then tr((p∘A)∘p) = Σ_i ⟨b_i, p(A(p b_i))⟩ (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner). Since p is self-adjoint (Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right), this is Σ_i ⟨p b_i, A(p b_i)⟩, which is 0 by step 1.
6. (Conclusion.) tangentialDivergence n M X x = g(x)·0 + Dg(x)(p(A x)) = Dg(x)((approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection(⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a)). ∎

Product rule: DX(x) = g(x)·A + Dg(x)(·)·A x.
tr(p∘DX(x)) = g(x)·tr(p∘A) + tr(u ↦ Dg(x)(u)·p(Ax)), and the rank-one trace equals Dg(x)(p(Ax)).
tr(p∘A) = tr(p∘A∘p) = Σ_i ⟨p b_i, A p b_i⟩ = 0, by idempotence, cyclicity, self-adjointness and skewness.

subproblem.title: C¹ angular test function adapted to the gap hypothesis
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a 2-dimensional linear subspace with orthogonal projection π := Q.starProjection, let a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a,e⟩ = 0, and let 0 < s ≤ 1/4. Let ψ, l ∈ C¹(ℝ) with tsupport ψ ⊆ (−s, s) and tsupport l ⊆ (1 − s, 1 + s). Put f(y) := arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩), A y := ⟨y,a⟩e − ⟨y,e⟩a, and Z := {y : ⟨y,a⟩ > 0, ||y| − 1| < s, |f(y)| < s, |y − πy| < s|y|}. Say that x satisfies the gap condition if ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s and |f(x)| < s together imply that |x − πx| < (s/2)|x| or 2s|x| < |x − πx|. Then there is a C¹ function g : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support such that, for every x satisfying the gap condition and every v ∈ ℝ^P with ⟨x,v⟩ = 0: Dg(x)v = ψ'(f(x))·l(|x|)·⟨Ax, v⟩/|πx|² if x ∈ Z, and Dg(x)v = 0 if x ∉ Z.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P) (s : ℝ) (ψ l : ℝ → ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → 0 < s → s ≤ 1 / 4 → ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ → ContDiff ℝ 1 l → tsupport ψ ⊆ Ioo (-s) s → tsupport l ⊆ Ioo (1 - s) (1 + s) → ∃ g : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ HasCompactSupport g ∧ (∀ x v : Euclid P, inner ℝ x v = 0 → (0 < inner ℝ x a → |‖x‖ - 1| < s → |Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)| < s → ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ < s / 2 * ‖x‖ ∨ 2 * s * ‖x‖ < ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖) → x ∈ {y : Euclid P | 0 < inner ℝ y a ∧ |‖y‖ - 1| < s ∧ |Real.arctan (inner ℝ y e / inner ℝ y a)| < s ∧ ‖y - Q.starProjection y‖ < s * ‖y‖} → fderiv ℝ g x v = deriv ψ (Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)) * l ‖x‖ * (inner ℝ (inner ℝ x a • e - inner ℝ x e • a) v / ‖Q.starProjection x‖ ^ 2)) ∧ (∀ x v : Euclid P, inner ℝ x v = 0 → (0 < inner ℝ x a → |‖x‖ - 1| < s → |Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)| < s → ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ < s / 2 * ‖x‖ ∨ 2 * s * ‖x‖ < ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖) → x ∉ {y : Euclid P | 0 < inner ℝ y a ∧ |‖y‖ - 1| < s ∧ |Real.arctan (inner ℝ y e / inner ℝ y a)| < s ∧ ‖y - Q.starProjection y‖ < s * ‖y‖} → fderiv ℝ g x v = 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4, 5 and 7 of the parent proof: the coefficient g = ψ(f)·l(|x|)·ζ of the rotation field and its derivative. The compact-support part of step 5 is carried out with the explicit compact set K below.
Notation: π := Q.starProjection; q(y) := y − πy; f(y) := arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩); A y := ⟨y,a⟩e − ⟨y,e⟩a; ψ' := deriv ψ; l' := deriv l; Ω := {y : ⟨y,a⟩ > 0}, which is open with 0 ∉ Ω; Z as in the statement. gap(x) denotes the implication [⟨x,a⟩ > 0 ∧ ||x|−1| < s ∧ |f(x)| < s] ⟹ [|q(x)| < (s/2)|x| ∨ 2s|x| < |q(x)|].
1. (Ingredients.) Apply Submission.idtp_cse_rc_cone_cutoff to (P, Q, s). It gives ζ with: (a) ζ is C¹ at every x ≠ 0; (b) ζ(x) = 1 if x ≠ 0 and |q(x)| ≤ (s/2)|x|; (c) ζ(x) = 0 if x ≠ 0 and s|x| ≤ |q(x)|; (d) Dζ(x) = 0 if x ≠ 0 and either |q(x)| < (s/2)|x| or s|x| < |q(x)|. Apply Submission.idtp_cse_rc_angle_fderiv to (P, Q, a, e). It gives (i) |πy|² = ⟨y,a⟩² + ⟨y,e⟩² for all y, and (ii) for ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, f is C¹ at x with Df(x)v = ⟨Ax, v⟩/|πx|².
2. (Definition.) h(y) := ψ(f(y))·l(|y|)·ζ(y). Set g(y) := h(y) if ⟨y,a⟩ > 0 and g(y) := 0 otherwise.
3. (Arctan bound.) If |arctan t| < s then |t| < 1. Indeed s ≤ 1/4 < π/4 since π ≥ 2. Also arctan 1 = π/4, arctan(−1) = −π/4, and arctan is strictly increasing. So −π/4 < arctan t < π/4 gives −1 < t < 1.
4. (Support bound.) If g(y) ≠ 0 then ⟨y,a⟩ ≥ 1/2 and |y| ≤ 5/4. Proof: g(y) ≠ 0 forces ⟨y,a⟩ > 0 (so y ≠ 0) and ψ(f(y)) ≠ 0, l(|y|) ≠ 0, ζ(y) ≠ 0. Hence f(y) ∈ tsupport ψ ⊆ (−s, s) and |y| ∈ tsupport l ⊆ (1 − s, 1 + s). Also |q(y)| < s|y|, since otherwise ζ(y) = 0 by (c). By step 3, |⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩| < 1, i.e. |⟨y,e⟩| < ⟨y,a⟩, so ⟨y,e⟩² < ⟨y,a⟩². Pythagoras gives |y|² = |πy|² + |q(y)|² (Submodule.norm_sq_eq_add_norm_sq_starProjection, with Qᗮ.starProjection y = y − πy). Hence |πy|² > |y|² − s²|y|² ≥ (15/16)|y|² > (15/16)(9/16), using s² ≤ 1/16 and |y| > 1 − s ≥ 3/4. By (i), |πy|² = ⟨y,a⟩² + ⟨y,e⟩² < 2⟨y,a⟩². Thus ⟨y,a⟩² > 135/512 > 1/4, and since ⟨y,a⟩ > 0, ⟨y,a⟩ > 1/2. Finally |y| < 1 + s ≤ 5/4.
5. (Compact support.) K := {y : 1/2 ≤ ⟨y,a⟩, |y| ≤ 5/4} is closed, being defined by non-strict inequalities between continuous functions, and contains {g ≠ 0} by step 4. So tsupport g = closure{g ≠ 0} ⊆ K ⊆ closedBall(0, 5/4). As a closed subset of a compact set, tsupport g is compact: HasCompactSupport g. Note that K ⊆ Ω.
6. (Local form.) If ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, then g = h on the open neighbourhood Ω of x. If ⟨x,a⟩ ≤ 0, then x ∉ K ⊇ tsupport g, so g = 0 on a neighbourhood of x (notMem_tsupport_iff_eventuallyEq); in particular Dg(x) = 0.
7. (g is C¹.) Let x ∈ Ω, so x ≠ 0. ψ∘f is C¹ at x since ψ ∈ C¹ and by (ii). y ↦ l(|y|) is C¹ at x since l ∈ C¹ and |·| is C^∞ away from 0 (contDiffAt_norm). ζ is C¹ at x by (a). So h is C¹ at x, and so is g, which equals h near x. For x ∉ Ω, g is locally the constant 0. Hence g is C¹ at every point: ContDiff ℝ 1 g (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt).
8. (Derivative on Ω.) Let ⟨x,a⟩ > 0 and ⟨x,v⟩ = 0. The norm is differentiable at x ≠ 0. Differentiating |y|² = (|y|)² at x and comparing with D(|·|²)(x)v = 2⟨x,v⟩ (hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq and uniqueness of derivatives) gives 2|x|·D|·|(x)v = 2⟨x,v⟩ = 0, so D|·|(x)v = 0. By the chain rule, D(ψ∘f)(x) = ψ'(f(x))·Df(x) and D(l∘|·|)(x) = l'(|x|)·D|·|(x). By the product rule for h = (ψ∘f)·(l∘|·|)·ζ and step 6, Dg(x)v = Dh(x)v = ψ(f(x))·l(|x|)·Dζ(x)v + ζ(x)·[ψ(f(x))·l'(|x|)·D|·|(x)v + l(|x|)·ψ'(f(x))·Df(x)v]. Therefore Dg(x)v = ψ(f(x))·l(|x|)·Dζ(x)v + ζ(x)·l(|x|)·ψ'(f(x))·Df(x)v. (★)
9. (First clause: x ∈ Z, gap(x), ⟨x,v⟩ = 0.) Here ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x|−1| < s, |f(x)| < s and |q(x)| < s|x|. gap(x) yields |q(x)| < (s/2)|x| or 2s|x| < |q(x)|. The second alternative is impossible because |q(x)| < s|x| < 2s|x| (|x| > 0). So |q(x)| < (s/2)|x|, and then ζ(x) = 1 by (b) and Dζ(x) = 0 by (d). With (★) and (ii), Dg(x)v = l(|x|)·ψ'(f(x))·⟨Ax,v⟩/|πx|² = ψ'(f(x))·l(|x|)·(⟨Ax,v⟩/|πx|²).
10. (Second clause: x ∉ Z, gap(x), ⟨x,v⟩ = 0.) If ⟨x,a⟩ ≤ 0, then Dg(x) = 0 by step 6. Otherwise use (★).
First term: if ψ(f(x)) ≠ 0 and l(|x|) ≠ 0, then f(x) ∈ (−s, s) and |x| ∈ (1 − s, 1 + s) by the support hypotheses. So gap(x) gives |q(x)| < (s/2)|x| or |q(x)| > 2s|x| > s|x|, and Dζ(x) = 0 by (d). Otherwise ψ(f(x))·l(|x|) = 0. Either way the first term is 0.
Second term: suppose ζ(x), l(|x|) and ψ'(f(x)) are all nonzero. ψ' vanishes off tsupport ψ (support_deriv_subset: ψ is 0 on the open complement of tsupport ψ), so f(x) ∈ tsupport ψ ⊆ (−s, s). Also |x| ∈ tsupport l ⊆ (1 − s, 1 + s), so ||x| − 1| < s, and |q(x)| < s|x| by (c). Then x ∈ Z, a contradiction. So the second term is 0, and Dg(x)v = 0.
11. g has all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take ζ from idtp_cse_rc_cone_cutoff and the formulas for |πy|² and Df from idtp_cse_rc_angle_fderiv.
Define g := ψ(f)·l(|·|)·ζ on Ω = {⟨y,a⟩ > 0} and g := 0 elsewhere.
g(y) ≠ 0 implies ⟨y,a⟩ > 1/2 and |y| < 5/4, so tsupport g ⊆ K = {⟨y,a⟩ ≥ 1/2, |y| ≤ 5/4} ⊆ Ω, which is compact.
g = h near points of Ω and g = 0 near points off Ω, so g is C¹.
For ⟨x,v⟩ = 0 the radial term drops: Dg(x)v = ψ(f)l·Dζ(x)v + ζ·l·ψ'(f)·Df(x)v.
The gap condition gives Dζ(x) = 0 where ψ(f)l ≠ 0; on Z, ζ = 1 and Df = ⟨Ax,·⟩/|πx|²; off Z, the ψ' term vanishes.
